extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in entertainment business and the comedy/festival industry (industry professionals, journalists, fans of Just For Laughs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for operating, preserving, monetizing, and expanding a major comedy festival/brand (Just For Laughs) through partnerships, programming choices, and distribution deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain domestic controlling stake to preserve subsidies
rubrics_metrics.description: Take and structure ownership stakes so the festival retains eligibility for government subsidies (e.g., Bell Media and Groupe CH took a controlling 51 percent stake to ensure continuing government subsidies for the Canadian-based comedy group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use majority domestic ownership where required by subsidy rules; structure consortium ownership to protect public funding streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate festival into broadcaster/platform ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate the festival into a parent company's media and events systems (e.g., 'integrate JFL into our system, to become part of our iHeartRadio events').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing channels (radio, TV, streaming, live-event arms) to create cross-promotional opportunities and extend reach across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and monetize recorded/digital specials
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner with broadcasters/streamers to produce one-hour comedy specials and other recorded content (e.g., CraveTV partnering with JFL to create one-hour comedy specials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn live festival programming into broadcast/streaming content to monetize intellectual property and provide programming for channels/streaming services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify festival programming toward one-person shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase emphasis on one-person shows and star-driven performances as part of festival programming (e.g., more one-person shows by stars like Kevin Hart, Jerry Seinfeld, Aziz Ansari).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program marquee solo shows to attract audiences and create sellable, tourable acts; balance these with other festival offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitally exploit the comedy brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue digital exploitation of the festival's brand to grow global business online (the group has targeted an increasingly global business online thanks to the digital age).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in digital distribution, social media, and online content strategies to expand audience and revenue beyond live events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand JFL-branded festivals to additional cities and territories
rubrics_metrics.description: Launch branded festivals in other cities and countries as a growth strategy (e.g., JFL-branded festivals in Toronto, Vancouver and Sydney, Australia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the core brand to create satellite events, tailoring programming and partnerships to local markets while leveraging central brand recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book major star talent to headline and legitimize events
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure high-profile comedians to host galas and bring one-man shows (examples: Tiffany Haddish, Trevor Noah, Kevin Hart) to drive attendance and publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize A-list talent for marquee slots to attract media attention, sponsors, and larger audiences; use star-driven programming to elevate festival profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble partners with complementary skills and resource commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a consortium of partners who each bring different skill sets and are willing to invest time and resources to ensure the festival's future (quote: 'each bring a different skill set, and each is investing the time and other resources to ensure a bright future').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose partners that cover broadcasting, event promotion, funding, and international expansion capabilities to create a resilient ownership/management structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve cultural identity while pursuing international expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance preserving the festival as a cultural treasure for its home country (e.g., 'preserve the comedy group as a cultural treasure for Canada') with ambitions to expand overseas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect elements of local cultural value and local stakeholder expectations even as you adapt programming and business models for international markets.
